newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PNG mulls banning overseas gold refining.
newsitem.headline: PNG mulls banning overseas gold refining.

text.p: Papua New Guinea may require gold miners to refine 100 percent of their gold ore inside the country under a proposal by acting prime minister John Giheno.

PNG already had a competitive refinery in Metals Refining Operation, said Giheno, adding that all gold and silver dore mined in PNG should be refined in the country, PNG's Post-Courier newspaper said on Friday.

"It's my firm belief that all gold and silver dore bars produced in Papua New Guinea should be refined onshore and marketed as high quality value added product," the newspaper quoted Giheno as saying.
"This will be of benefit through increased employment and business activities as well as increasing the value of our gold exports," said Giheno.
Giheno was mines and energy minister until he became acting prime minister after PNG's recent political upheaval.
Metals Refining Operation Pty Ltd is 45 percent owned by Golden West Refining Corp Ltd which is 50 percent owned by Rothschild Australia Ltd.

Golden West managing director Michael Ryan said the requirement would have only a minimal impact on refining on PNG gold mining sector, since a large portion of the 1.6 million ounces of gold produced by PNG already is refined internally.
The exception is the Porgera mine, operated jointly by Placer Dome Inc, with 50 percent and RGC Ltd and agencies of the PNG government, each with 25 percent.
"All but the 70 percent of Porgera already is refined in PNG," Ryan said.
Gold dore from the Misima mine, 80 percent owned by Placer, is refined entirely in PNG, Ryan said.

However, Giheno's proposal could have implications for Lihir Gold Ltd, which this week reached agreement with Metals Refining and Rothschild to refine future production from the Lihir gold project in PNG and elsewhere using a syndicate of overseas refineries.
Lihir expects to produce 175,000 ounces of gold this year, rising to over 550,000 ounces in 1998.
A spokeswoman for Gold Corp of Australia, which operates the Perth Mint, said that although it currently did not refine any PNG gold, a ban on overseas refining would be "disappointing."
Gold Corp would like to retain the opportunity to tender for future refining work from PNG, she said.
Indonesia already maintains a ban on overseas refining of gold.
